DEVELOP THE BASIS FOR A MEDICARE STRATEGY
THE FOLLOWING SUBTASKS PROVIDE THE BASIS FOR A STRATEGY FOR CONTINUING TO GROW MA, WHICH OFFERS THE
POTENTIAL TO SLOW LONG-TERM MEDICARE COST GROWTH AND INCREASE COORDINATED CARE DELIVERY WITH HIGHERVALUE
PROVIDERS, THEREBY IMPROVING PATIENT OUTCOMES. MA ENROLLEES AS A PERCENT OF MEDICARE
BENEFICIARIES CONTINUE TO GROW (31% OF ALL MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES IN 2016, UP FROM 25% IN 2011 AND
22% IN 2008) AND CURRENT PROJECTIONS BY THE CBO SUGGEST THAT WITHOUT ANY OTHER CHANGES, BY 2026 41%
OF MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES WILL BE ENROLLED IN AN MA PLAN. UNDER CURRENT POLICY, PRIVATE MA PLANS
TYPICALLY DELIVER BASIC MEDICARE BENEFITS AT A LOWER COST THAN FFS DOES. INCREASING MA PENETRATION
WOULD POTENTIALLY LOWER MEDICARE COSTS AND PROVIDE CMS WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO WORK WITH MA PLANS
ON VALUE-BASED CAPITATION ARRANGEMENTS.

OBJECTIVES

ELEMENTS
■ UNDERSTAND CONSUMER DECISION-MAKING IN MA PLAN SELECTION

OBJECTIVES
■ ASSESS LEVERS AGAINST FRAMEWORK, INCLUDING ASSESSING RELATIVE IMPACT, Â€ŒCOSTSÂ€?, AND IMPLEMENTATION
FEASIBILITY OF DIFFERENT INTERVENTIONS
■ TEST REGULATORY CONSTRAINTS WITH CMS LEGAL COUNSEL

OBJECTIVES
■ IDENTIFY SET OF HIGH-LEVEL IMPLEMENTATION OPTIONS
■ DEVELOP HIGH-LEVEL COMMUNICATIONS STRATEGY
PRIORITIZE THE BASIS FOR A MEDICARE PRODUCT COMPETITIVE BIDDING STRATEGY
THE FOLLOWING SUBTASKS PROVIDE THE BASIS FOR A STRATEGY FOR CONTINUING TO FOSTER INNOVATION IN MA. OVER
THE PAST FEW YEARS, MEDICARE ADVANTAGE PLANS HAVE PURSUED INNOVATIONS IN PROVIDER PAYMENT THROUGH

THEIR ABILITY TO MARKET TO AND COMMUNICATE WITH BENEFICIARIES.

OBJECTIVES

MEDICARE COULD ALSO ENCOURAGE DEMAND-SIDE INNOVATION, WHICH COULD BE OF VALUE BUT ALSO PROVIDE A COMPOUNDING BENEFIT COUPLED WITH PAYMENT INNOVATIONS ALREADY UNDERWAY.  CMS HAS TAKEN SOME INITIAL STEPS, FOR EXAMPLE THROUGH THE CENTERS FOR MEDICARE AND MEDICAID INNOVATION (CMMI) LAUNCHING A PILOT IN VALUE-BASED INSURANCE DESIGN (VBID) FOR A LIMITED SET OF QUALIFYING MA PLANS AS OF JANUARY 2017. BOTH COMPONENTS OF THE OFFICE HAVE EXPERIENCED ENHANCED INTEREST IN AND OVERSIGHT OF THEIR PROGRAMS OVER THE LAST TWO YEARS, AS WELL AS AN INCREASED DEMAND ON PROGRAM OPERATIONS AND STAFF.

DURING THE MONTHS OF MAY-JULY 2014, THERE WAS A SIGNIFICANT AND UNPRECEDENTED SURGE IN THE NUMBER OF
CHILDREN REFERRED TO THE UC PROGRAM. ORR AND THE UC PROGRAM ENTERED THE SURGE WITH AN EXTREMELY LEAN STAFFED ORGANIZATION. THIS WAS A REFLECTION OF A NUMBER OF FACTORS: AMONG OTHERS, THE RAPID EXPANSION OF THE PROGRAM IN THE TWO YEARS PRIOR TO THE 2014 SURGE, DURING WHICH UC REFERRALS AND THE PROGRAMÂ€™S BUDGET ROSE SIGNIFICANTLY; DIFFICULTIES IN HIRING DUE TO FEDERAL BUDGETARY RESTRICTIONS AND HIRING FREEZES, AS WELL AS THE UC PROGRAMÂ€™S HISTORIC RELIANCE ON GRANTEES TO PERFORM MOST SERVICE RESPONSIBILITIES. THE NUMBER OF REFERRALS FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) MORE THAN DOUBLED EACH FISCAL YEAR BEGINNING IN FY2011, TO 57,496 IN FY2014. DURING THIS TIME, THE PROGRAMÂ€™S BUDGET ALSO INCREASED FROM APPROXIMATELY $150 MILLION IN FY2011 TO OVER $912 MILLION IN FY2014. HOWEVER, SINCE FY2011, THE PROGRAM HAD MANAGED WITH A MODESTLY INCREASING NUMBER OF FTEÂ€™S, FROM APPROXIMATELY 40 IN FY2012 TO 48 IN FY2013 AND 56 IN FY2014.

IN ADDITION TO THE SIGNIFICANT EXPANSION OF THE UC PROGRAM, ORRÂ€™S MANDATE TO SERVE OTHER POPULATIONS,
INCLUDING REFUGEES, SPECIAL IMMIGRANT VISA HOLDERS, ASYLEES, CUBAN/HAITIAN ENTRANTS, VICTIMS OF TORTURE, AND UNACCOMPANIED REFUGEE MINORS HAS ALSO EXPANDED IN RECENT YEARS. THESE ACTIVITIES REQUIRE ENHANCED
COORDINATION WITH OTHER FEDERAL AND NON-FEDERAL PARTNERS AND OPERATE IN THE CONTEXT OF A LIMITED BUDGET AND ENHANCED OVERSIGHT.

IN FY2014 AND FY2015, ACF APPROVED AND RECRUITED FOR 72 NEW ORR POSITIONS, AS WELL AS TWO MEDICAL STAFF POSITIONS, FOR A TOTAL OF 74 ADDITIONAL UC STAFF. THIS LEVEL OF STAFFING IS PROJECTED TO SUPPORT AN ANNUAL REFERRAL LEVEL OF 58,000. THE NEW POSITIONS INCLUDE FIELD SPECIALISTS, PROJECT OFFICERS, PROGRAM SPECIALISTS,
COMMISSIONED CORPS OFFICERS FOCUSING ON HEALTH, AND NEW POLICY AND DATA POSITIONS. ALL OF THESE NEW STAFF
ARE NOW IN PLACE.

SIMILARLY, IN 2014 THE DIVISION OF REFUGEE ASSISTANCE SHIFTED THE HEADQUARTERS-ONLY STAFFING STRUCTURE TO
INCLUDE REGIONAL REPRESENTATIVES, HOUSED IN THE TEN (10) HHS REGIONAL OFFICES AROUND THE COUNTRY. ORR
CREATED A POLICY DIVISION WITHIN THE OFFICE OF THE DIRECTOR TO ADVISE ORR LEADERSHIP ON POLICY DEVELOPMENT
AND COMMUNICATION ACROSS ORR PROGRAMS. IN ADDITION, A RENEWED EMPHASIS ON MONITORING, COMPLIANCE AND OVERSIGHT IN THE REFUGEE PROGRAMS HAS SEEN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A NEW TEAM OF CONTRACT MONITORS IN FY2016. THE RECENT ANNOUNCEMENT OF AN ADDITIONAL 10,000 REFUGEES EXPECTED TO BE SERVED IN FY2016 WILL REQUIRE STAFF TO CONTINUE BUILDING ON PROGRAM EFFICIENCIES AND BEST PRACTICES TO MEET THE GOALS OF THE OFFICE.

GIVEN THESE SIGNIFICANT CHANGES IN THE ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE OF ORR, A FORMAL ORGANIZATIONAL REVIEW WILL PROVIDE NEEDED ANALYSIS AND INSIGHT INTO THE FUNCTIONALITY AND EFFICIENCY OF THE CURRENT OPERATIONAL STRUCTURE, AS WELL AS IDENTIFY AREAS OF IMPROVEMENTS OR GAPS NOT YET ADDRESSED THROUGH STAFFING OR MANAGEMENT CHANGES.
